checks.note: There are exactly three days: Day 1 is Mile End and the Plateau, Day 2 is Old Montreal and Little Burgundy, and Day 3 is Jean-Talon Market, the Botanical Garden and Little Italy. No extra or missing days.

Food is central throughout. Every part of Days 1 and 2 has a named food stop. Day 3 morning has Alati-Caserta and Jean-Talon Market, and Day 3 evening has Impasto. Only the Day 3 afternoon (Botanical Garden) has no food stop, which still leaves a named food stop in most parts of each day.

Most costs are moderate: bagels $3–8, Schwartz's $15–25, market lunches $10–20, Impasto $30–50. There is one splurge (Joe Beef, $90–150+), and the cheaper Liverpool House is offered as an alternative. This fits a mid-range budget.

October is well covered. The plan includes fall foliage stops and peak-colour caveats, short daylight with sunset times, and correctly dates Canadian Thanksgiving to Oct 12, 2026. It also notes seasonal market thinning and gives a rainy-day swap for each day.

Every stop is a specific real place with a plausible address, e.g. St-Viateur Bagel, Fairmount Bagel, Schwartz's (3895 St-Laurent), La Banquise (994 Rachel E), Dieu du Ciel!, Olive et Gourmando, Atwater Market, Joe Beef, Liverpool House, Alati-Caserta, Jean-Talon Market and Impasto.

unasked_content: The 'verify' and 'I couldn't confirm' caveats are repeated many times (in the opening assumptions, inline at several stops, and again at the end). This makes the plan longer and less confident without adding useful information.
The note that Bixi bike stations and patios wind down by mid-November is outside the October trip window, so it doesn't help this traveller.
